from.place: Lemma 05SA(2): values of LF are functorial on morphisms

title: Left derived values are functorial
statement: In Situation 05S8 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of $\mathcal D$ such that $LF$ is defined at $X$ and at $Y$. Then there is a unique morphism $LF(f):LF(X)\to LF(Y)$ between the values such that for every commutative square $f\circ s=s'\circ f'$ with $s:X'\to X$ and $s':Y'\to Y$ in $S$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, the diagram formed by $LF(X)\to F(X')\to F(X)$, $LF(Y)\to F(Y')\to F(Y)$ (the first arrows being the cone maps of the essentially constant pro-objects) and the vertical maps $LF(f)$, $F(f')$, $F(f)$ commutes.
